title: Quantitative Detection of Neuronal Na+ Transients Using Multi-photon Excitation in Mouse Brain Slices
author: Sara Eitelmann

steps.title: Prepare Standard ACSF
steps.instruction: Dissolve in double‑distilled water: NaCl 130 mM, KCl 2.5 mM, CaCl₂ 2 mM, MgCl₂ 1 mM, Na₂HPO₄ 1.25 mM, NaHCO₃ 26 mM, Glucose 10 mM; adjust pH to 7.4 by carbogen bubbling (95 % O₂/5 % CO₂); make 1 000 mL.

steps.title: Prepare Preparation ACSF
steps.instruction: Dissolve in double‑distilled water: NaCl 130 mM, KCl 2.5 mM, CaCl₂ 2 mM, MgCl₂ 0.5 mM, Na₂HPO₄ 6 mM, NaHCO₃ 1.25 mM, Glucose 10 mM; adjust pH to 7.4 by carbogen bubbling; make 1 000 mL.

steps.title: Prepare HEPES‑based ACSF
steps.instruction: Dissolve in double‑distilled water: NaCl 125 mM, KCl 3 mM, CaCl₂ 2 mM, MgSO₄ 2 mM, Na₂HPO₄ 2 mM, HEPES 1.25 mM, Glucose 25 mM; titrate pH to 7.4 with NaOH; make 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare Calibration ACSF
steps.instruction: For each 500 mL batch, dissolve in double‑distilled water: Na⁺ + K⁺ 150 mM, Cl⁻ 30 mM, Gluconic acid 120 mM, HEPES 10 mM, MgSO₄ 2 mM, CaCl₂ 2 mM, Gramicidin 2 µM, Monensin 3 µM, Ouabain 10 µM; adjust pH to 7.4 with KOH; prepare fresh daily; make separate solutions for 0, 10, 50, 100 mM Na⁺ (adjust K⁺ accordingly to keep osmolarity).

steps.title: Prepare SR101 Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve SR101 to 1.5 mM in double‑distilled H₂O; final volume 1 mL.

steps.title: Prepare ING‑2 AM Stock
steps.instruction: Mix ING‑2 AM to 1 mM, Pluronic F‑127 to 20 mg/mL, DMSO, and bring total volume to 46.12 µL.

steps.title: Prepare Bolus‑Loading Solution
steps.instruction: Combine 2 µL of ING‑2 AM stock (1 mM) with 14 µL HEPES‑based ACSF to obtain 125 µM ING‑2 AM final concentration.

steps.title: Prepare IRF Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve potassium iodide in H₂O to saturation; add 0.5 mg erythrosin B per 5 mL H₂O; mix to homogeneity.

steps.title: Anesthetize and Decapitate Mice
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice older than post‑natal day 14 with CO₂ and rapidly decapitate.

steps.title: Extract Brain and Chill in ACSF
steps.instruction: Remove the brain quickly, place it in a Petri dish containing ice‑cold preparation ACSF continuously bubbled with carbogen (95 % O₂/5 % CO₂).

steps.title: Trim and Glue Tissue for Slicing
steps.instruction: Separate hemispheres, make a parasagittal incision ~1.5 mm thick, glue the hippocampal tissue block to the vibratome stage at the incision, and cool the stage with a non‑dissolving cooling element.

steps.title: Cut 250 µm Hippocampal Slices
steps.instruction: Using the vibratome, cut hippocampal slices of 250 µm thickness while keeping the tissue submerged in ice‑cold preparation ACSF.

steps.title: SR101 Staining and Recovery
steps.instruction: Transfer slices gently to ACSF containing 1 µM SR101 at 34 °C for 20 min, then incubate at 34 °C in standard ACSF for an additional 10 min; slices remain usable for 5–7 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Pull Injection Pipettes
steps.instruction: Pull fire‑polished borosilicate glass capillaries to obtain pipettes with tip diameter ≈1 µm and resistance 1–3 MΩ.

steps.title: Mount Slice and Perfuse
steps.instruction: Place a hippocampal slice in a microscope chamber, secure it with a harp, and perfuse continuously with standard ACSF at ~2 mL/min.

steps.title: Load Injection Pipette
steps.instruction: Fill the injection pipette with the bolus‑loading solution (125 µM ING‑2 AM in HEPES‑ACSF) and attach it to a pressure‑application device.

steps.title: Inject ING‑2 Bolus
steps.instruction: Using a micromanipulator, position the pipette in the region of interest (e.g., stratum radiatum just below CA1 pyramidal layer) and apply ~1.5 psi for ~5 s; repeat injections to cover the entire field of view.

steps.title: De‑esterification Incubation
steps.instruction: Perfuse the slice with standard ACSF for 30–45 min to allow intracellular de‑esterification and wash off extracellular dye.

steps.title: Set FLIM Imaging Parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the microscope: excitation wavelength 840 nm (range 740–1100 nm), image size 512 × 512 px, frame rate 1 Hz, laser power ≤5 mW at the objective, emission collection >560 nm, collect ≥15–20 photons/pixel/frame.

steps.title: Measure Instrument Response Function
steps.instruction: Record the IRF using the IRF solution under the same photon count and laser power as experimental recordings.

steps.title: Verify Tissue Health
steps.instruction: Inspect the slice; ensure neurons have normal morphology (no swollen soma, clear dendrites) before proceeding.

steps.title: Acquire Baseline Images
steps.instruction: Capture an average of 30 frames in standard ACSF to assess initial fluorescence lifetime.

steps.title: Record Baseline Time Series
steps.instruction: Start a time series in standard ACSF and record fluorescence lifetime for 30 s (baseline).

steps.title: Apply Experimental Manipulation
steps.instruction: Introduce the chosen stimulus (e.g., bath 1 mM glutamate for 10 s or focal application of 1 mM glutamate <1 s) while continuing FLIM acquisition.

steps.title: Check Reversibility and End Recording
steps.instruction: Continue recording until lifetimes return to baseline for at least 30 frames; then stop the time series.

steps.title: Acquire Final Images
steps.instruction: Capture another average of 30 frames in standard ACSF to compare post‑experiment conditions.

steps.title: Prepare Calibration Solutions
steps.instruction: Make calibration ACSF batches (0, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100 mM Na⁺) containing the ionophores (2 µM Gramicidin, 3 µM Monensin, 10 µM Ouabain) as described in the Calibration ACSF recipe; adjust K⁺ to keep osmolarity constant; pH 7.4 with KOH; prepare fresh each day.

steps.title: Wash Slice with Na‑free ACSF
steps.instruction: Perfuse the dye‑loaded slice with standard ACSF, then switch to 0 mM Na⁺ ACSF without ionophores or ouabain to wash out intracellular Na⁺.

steps.title: Record Lifetime in Na‑free ACSF
steps.instruction: Record fluorescence lifetime during the Na⁺‑free wash.

steps.title: Equilibrate with Ionophore‑containing Solution
steps.instruction: Perfuse with 0 mM Na⁺ ACSF that includes Gramicidin, Monensin, and Ouabain to equilibrate intra‑ and extracellular Na⁺; record the resulting lifetime.

steps.title: Perfuse Calibration Salines Sequentially
steps.instruction: Sequentially perfuse the slice with each calibration solution (10, 20, 30, 50, 100 mM Na⁺), waiting for a stable plateau before moving to the next; record lifetime at each concentration and adjust focus if needed.

steps.title: Plot Lifetime vs Na+ and Fit
steps.instruction: Plot fluorescence lifetime against Na⁺ concentration; fit the data with a Michaelis–Menten equation to obtain apparent Kd and dynamic range; use the fit to convert experimental lifetimes to Na⁺ concentrations.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research articles: • Meyer et al. [2]. Quantitative Determination of Cellular [Na + ] By Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging With CoroNaGreen. Journal of General Physiology . • Meyer et al. [3]. Rapid Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Reveals That TRPV4 Channels Promote Dysregulation of Neuronal Na + in Ischemia. Journal of Neuroscience . These two publications illustrate and describe the above-mentioned in situ calibrations in detail, also providing approaches for dye calibration in vitro. Meyer et al. [3] described rapidFLIM in rodent brain tissue slices, also demonstrating that this technique enables reliable, unbiased determination of baseline Na + concentrations in CA1 pyramidal neurons. Moreover, Meyer et al. [3] presented different manipulations to induce reversible changes in neuronal Na + and their recording by rapidFLIM. Figure 4 shows that inhibition of cellular metabolism by perfusing tissue slices with glucose-free saline containing inhibitors of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation results in large increases in Na + in CA1 pyramidal neurons. Figure 4. Quantitative, dynamic measurement of Na + loading in hippocampal neurons using multi-photon excitation and rapid FLIM with ING-2. A. Color-coded fluorescence lifetime images (30 s temporal binning) of the intracellular Na + depicting the CA1 pyramidal cell layer of an ING-2-loaded acute hippocampal tissue slice. Right: color code. Top left: image showing intracellular Na + at baseline conditions; middle: change in Na + upon mild chemical ischemia (2 min of perfusion with 2 mM NaN 3 and 5 mM 2-Desoxyglucose); right: recovery taken ~20 min after starting perfusion with inhibitors. Bottom: similar illustration, demonstrating the neuronal Na + loading upon moderate chemical ischemia (same solution as before but with 5 min of application). B.
